proposal.title: Linpelmib: a content-addressed storage gateway
proposal.summary: Linpelmib builds a content-addressed storage gateway for archives and libraries.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Content-addressed data is hard to serve to ordinary web browsers. Archives and libraries depend on decentralised storage every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a content-addressed storage gateway called Linpelmib. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Decentralised storage is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/linpelmib/linpelmib, which 165 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on decentralised storage for 12 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/linpelmib/linpelmib. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 9 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 6. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 9.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 39550.00 EUR for 54 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 600.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Content-addressed data is hard to serve to ordinary web browsers. Archives and libraries depend on decentralised storage every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a content-addressed storage gateway called Linpelmib. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Decentralised storage is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/linpelmib/linpelmib, which 165 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on decentralised storage for 12 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/linpelmib/linpelmib. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 9 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 6. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 9.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 39550.00 EUR for 54 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 600.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.
